title: Tasklet Assembly — rough PRD & idea pad
content:
Context / why this exists:
- We keep building small helper flows (greeting, disambiguation, price-check) and reimplementing glue every time. Engineers want composable building blocks they can wire into a conversation or a server-side workflow.
- Goal: make a lightweight in-console composer for small, versioned 'tasklets' (1-3 intent steps) that are reusable across routes, can be executed server-side or injected client-side, and are instrumented for cost/latency.

Problem statement:
- Repetition: teams copy-paste prompt snippets and orchestration glue (API calls, input validation, fallbacks).
- Hard to audit: no centralized registry, no easy way to rollback or apply fixes globally.
- Onboarding friction: new engineers do not know which micro-flows exist; they re-create behavior leading to user-visible regressions.

High-level feature idea (sketch):
- Tasklet = small declarative spec that includes: metadata (name, owner, tags, version), matching trigger (route or explicit call), steps (prompt templates / functions to call / validations), inputs/outputs contract (shape + example), runtime hints (fidelity tier, timeout, preferred model variants).
- Console UI: list / search / create / quick-insert into prompt editor. Visual composer for simple linear flows (drag reorder steps).
- Runtime: tasklets are stored in control plane; when invoked, the router substitutes and executes with configured model variant + runtime hints. Support both inline expansion (client) and remote execution (server).
- Versioning & rollout: bump versions, canaries, rollback to earlier version, diff view.

User personas:
- Product engineer (PLG team) — wants to reuse a disambiguation step across two assistant flows without involving infra.
- Solutions engineer — assemble a chain of tool calls + LLM prompts for a customer PoC and later lock the artifact for managed rollout.
- Platform owner — audit who changed a tasklet, collect perf/cost metrics, and push fixes globally.

User stories (MVP):
- As a product engineer I can create a tasklet that validates a user email and returns a canonical form. Acceptance: UI to author a template + unit test harness that runs an example input and shows output.
- As a product engineer I can insert an existing tasklet into a route's prompt; when the route executes, the tasklet runs and the route receives the normalized output. Acceptance: route logs show the tasklet id/version and output contract adhered to.
- As a platform owner I can roll a tasklet update to 10% of traffic and monitor cost and latency. Acceptance: rollout controls in Console, metrics per-version.

Non-functional / constraints:
- Tasklets must have a small spec surface — keep first pass to template + function-call + simple JSON schema for IO. No complex branching or loops in MVP.
- Runtime cost: prefer remote execution for heavy prompts to avoid token duplication at client. Add caching for idempotent outputs.
- Security: tasklets that call external functions must be auditable and require higher permission to publish.

Instrumentation & metrics:
- Per-tasklet: invocation count, p50/p95 latency, avg tokens consumed, error rate, cost per 1k calls.
- Version delta metrics: ability to compare v1 vs v2 on latency/cost/quality on a shared eval set.

Prototype technical notes (spikes):
- Storage model: store tasklet spec as JSON in control plane with content-addressed id + simple ACL.
- Execution path: router receives route request -> if tasklet configured for inline expansion, fetch spec, render template, either execute via same model selection path or call into tasklet runner service.
- Caching layer: key = (tasklet id, inputs hash, model+variant); TTL configurable per-tasklet.
- Eval harness: small runner to replay a set of inputs across versions and compute quality regressions (BLEU-like heuristics + manual checks).

Console UX rough flow:
- Tasklets home: search, filters by tags, owner, route usage, recent failures.
- Compose screen: title, tags, input schema (JSON schema text area), steps list (each step: type {prompt | function-call}, prompt editor, example input/output), runtime hints.
- Quick-insert: in route prompt editor, type /tasklet -> shows matching tasklets; choose: inline vs remote execution.

Rollout + governance:
- Publish workflow: draft -> request review (optional) -> publish (default private to team) -> promote to org/shared.
- Permissions: create/edit/publish scopes; ability to lock a tasklet (no edits without admin).

Success metrics (first 3 months after launch):
- 30+ distinct tasklets authored across platform teams.
- 40% reduction in duplicated prompt snippets in a random sample of routes.
- Latency increase <= 5% for routes that adopt remote execution (compared to baseline).
- Alerting on regressions: at least one regression detected and rolled back via versioning.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How much expressivity before tasklets become mini-scripts? Keep MVP intentionally small.
- Where to put enforcement for IO schema — at compile-time (console) or runtime (runner)? Both have tradeoffs.
- Internationalization: templating needs to support locale variables; may defer.
- Billing model: should tasklet invocations count as route tokens or separate meter? Discuss with finance.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Quick spike: build a "validate-email" tasklet prototype and hook into one low-risk route (internal help bot). Owner: Kevin. Timebox: 2 weeks.
- UX mockups: hand off to Maya for simple compose flow. Deliverable: 3 screens. Timebox: 1 week.
- Infra spike: small runner that can execute a prompt template + function call + record metrics. Owner: Ishaan. Timebox: 2 weeks.
- Confluence doc: flesh out governance + permission model (link above).

Notes / random thoughts (scratchpad):
- Could expose tasklets as npm-like package with semantic versions for teams that want to vendor them. Maybe later.
- Consider a tiny marketplace of vetted community tasklets (only if we can moderate).
- Nice-to-have: preview diff that shows token delta when swapping in a tasklet (estimate cost impact).

-- end --
